exposure: subsequent delivery mode (elective repeat Caesarean section, trial of labour after Caesarean section)
outcome: maternal morbidity (adhesions, obliteration of utero-vesical fold)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 942 women with a history of previous Caesarean section admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology.
finding: Among women with a previous Caesarean section, 530 underwent elective repeat CS and 412 attempted trial of labour (TOLAC), resulting in 311 successful vaginal deliveries and 96 emergency repeat CS, with maternal morbidity at 11.25%, maternal mortality at 0.15%, perinatal morbidity at 3.32%, and perinatal mortality at 3.96%.
mod_finding: Among women with a previous Caesarean section, a trial of labour after Caesarean section led to successful vaginal delivery in 311 out of 412 cases (75.5%) and required emergency repeat Caesarean section in 96 cases (23.3%).
